battle.name: 亞述內戰
battle.theater: 底格里斯河上游亞述核心區
battle.brief: 公元前十八世紀中葉，亞述出現雙王並存的局面：馬茲王系的阿舒爾-貝尼-伊提與爭奪王位的亞馬尼-貝尼-阿達德相鬥，核心城阿舒爾的加冕權成了勝負所在。此役無戰報可考，只靠尼尼微出土的兩塊國王石碑與哈納努致亞述王的書信追出輪廓；卡面這件埃及長矛，正是同一時代近東步兵手中的標準持械。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的兩方都自稱亞述王，差別只在王系。亞述王位分為兩支：馬茲王系（以馬茲為據點，承繼沙姆希-阿達德一世與伊什梅-達甘一世的血統）與尼斯王系（以尼努瓦，即泰爾巴塞特基為根據，君主名號多帶「伊什梅」或「沙姆希」）。這兩支在公元前十八世紀中葉約四十五年間同時稱王，分據底格里斯河上游的亞述心臟地，聖城阿舒爾的加冕權是雙方爭奪的關鍵。亞述的邊境之外是一圈緩衝國：胡里人統治的哈納國（哈蘭）由哈納努執掌，幼發拉底中游的埃馬爾、扎爾帕爾等城邦名義上臣服，實際上各行其是；西面是強盛的亞姆哈德王國（阿勒頗），再往西是米坦尼；南方是加斯底特王朝的巴比倫，東南方是埃蘭，安納托利亞的赫梯老王國亦已式微。埃及第十八王朝正處於阿馬爾納時期，亞述王阿舒爾-烏巴里德一世在阿馬爾納書信中與底比斯往返，年代與這場內戰重疊。指揮系統方面，此時亞述並無成熟的將軍團：國王自領一軍，另有城邑守將與部落民兵首領；命令靠口信與信差傳遞，盟友與附庸各自出兵，兩大王系之間並無統一的作戰序列。
countriesEn: Both sides claimed to be king of Assyria; the difference lay in the royal line. The Assyrian kingship had split into two houses: the Mazi house, based at Mazi and descended from Shamshi-Adad I and Ishme-Dagan I, and the Nis house, based at Ninuua, modern Tell Bassetki, whose rulers bore names containing Ishme or Shamshi. For roughly forty-five years in the middle of the eighteenth century BC these two lines held the title of king at the same time, each occupying a different part of the Assyrian heartland in the upper Tigris, and the right to be crowned in the sacred city of Assur was the prize they fought over. Around Assyria lay a ring of buffer states. The Hurrian-ruled kingdom of Khana, centred on Harran, was governed by Hananu; the Euphrates cities of Emar and Zalpar claimed submission while in practice followed their own course. To the west lay the powerful kingdom of Yamhad, that is Aleppo, and beyond it Mitanni. To the south was Babylon under the Kassite dynasty, to the south-east Elam, and in the west Anatolia, where the Hittite Old Kingdom was already in decline. Egypt's Eighteenth Dynasty was in the Amarna age, and the Assyrian king Ashur-uballit I corresponded with Thebes in the Amarna letters, dating from exactly the same stretch of years as this civil war. As for command, Assyria at this time had no mature corps of generals: the king led one army in person, alongside city commanders and the heads of tribal levies. Orders travelled by word of mouth and by messenger, allied and vassal contingents each raised their own men, and there was no combined order of battle linking the two royal houses.
people: 留下姓名的只有寥寥數人，正因為少，每一個都重要。馬茲王系的末代君主阿舒爾-貝尼-伊提是內戰的直接受害者：其父阿舒爾-貝利-烏蘇爾死後，他承襲亞述王位，在位多年卻始終未能真正壓倒對面的王系；他的黑玄武岩石碑於二十世紀中葉在尼尼微出土，碑文自述平定內亂，語氣是獲勝者的一邊。另一塊同樣出自尼尼微的石碑屬於亞馬尼-貝尼-阿達德——他以親屬身分起兵反叛，一度奪取王位並奪走阿舒爾-貝尼-伊提的性命，卻最終敗於對方王系。終結這場內戰的是尼斯王系的阿舒爾-尼拉里一世（又名伊什梅-卡利-盧，父為阿舒爾-馬基爾），他在阿舒爾-貝尼-伊提被殺之後登上王位，收拾殘局，讓亞述重新回到一個王、一座聖城的秩序裡。域外最關鍵的旁觀者是哈納國王哈納努：他致亞述王的書信提到自己的城邑被鄰國奪走而求助無門，更提到「另一位王」的存在，成為學界判定亞述同時存在兩位國王的最硬文獻。同期還有亞姆哈德王這位亞述在西方的競爭者，以及埃及底比斯的阿門荷特普三世與阿肯那頓，雙方在外交場合多次談及「亞述之王」的名號與軍力。
peopleEn: Only a handful of names survive, and precisely because they are so few each one matters. The last ruler of the Mazi house, Ashur-beni-iti, was the direct victim of the war: after the death of his father Ashur-beli-usur he inherited the Assyrian throne and reigned for many years without ever truly crushing the opposing line. His basalt stele was excavated at Nineveh in the middle of the twentieth century, and its text recounts the pacification of the civil strife in the tone of the side that had won. A matching stele from the same city at Nineveh belongs to Yamani-beni-Adad, who rose in revolt as a kinsman, seized the throne for a time and took the life of Ashur-beni-iti, but was in the end defeated by the other house. The man who ended the war was Ashur-nirari I of the Nis house, also called Ishme-kali-lu, son of Ashur-makir. He took the throne in the aftermath of the killing of Ashur-beni-iti, tidied up what was left of the kingdom and returned Assyria to an order of one king and one sacred city. The most important witness outside the country was Hananu, king of Khana. His letter to the king of Assyria tells how one of his towns had been seized by a neighbour and how his appeals went unanswered, and it refers explicitly to the existence of the other king; it is the hardest piece of evidence for the judgement that Assyria had two kings at once. The same years also saw the king of Yamhad, Assyria's rival in the west, and in Egypt the Theban pharaohs Amenhotep III and Akhenaten, whose diplomatic circles several times discussed the name and the military weight of the king of Assyria.
kits: 卡面上這件埃及長矛，是早王朝就已定型的直刃長矛：銅或青銅矛頭以榫口或縛紮固定在木杆上，杆長及肩。放到公元前十八世紀的近東，這種形制並未過時：它既是埃及步兵的制式長矛，也正是兩河各城邦步卒最普遍的主兵器，亞述的步兵大概率也用同類銅矛——只是亞述此期的考古出土極少，出土銅矛頭多見於泰爾比拉、哈薩努等鄰近地區，可作旁證而非直接證據。亞述此期的常見裝備可由器物類型拼出大樣：銅斧（窄身斧刃、配木柄）為劈砍之用；銅匕首與彎刃短劍用於近身格鬥；弓在兩河於此時已出現複合弓形制，箭鏈多為銅或骨，但亞述境內的實物稀少，說明其遠程火力仍以投擲器與輕兵器為主；盾牌多為木胎蒙皮，圓形為主，長形盾在此期尚不多見。此時尚無成建制的鎧甲與頭盔——亞述的青銅頭盔要到新亞述時期才大量出現於王陵與浮雕。攻城器械方面，這一時期的亞述有過圍城與破城的記載常見於埃馬爾等敘利亞文書，提到土坡、撞槌與火攻，但內戰本身沒有留下攻城細節。馬匹在亞述的用途仍以駕車與乘騎為主，雙輪輕車是兩河貴族的標配，軍中馬數有限，騎兵並非決定兵種。運輸方面，舊亞述時期商隊靠驢隊往返安納托利亞與亞述，每段約一百公里；而到內戰年代，銅與錫的商路已因胡里人勢力北進而中斷，這一點直接影響軍隊的裝備補充。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is a straight-bladed weapon whose form was already fixed in the Early Dynastic period: a copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by socket or lashing, the shaft reaching to the shoulder. Set in the Near East of the eighteenth century BC this form was not out of date: it was both the standard spear of the Egyptian infantry and the commonest main arm of the infantry of the Mesopotamian city-states, and the Assyrian foot very probably carried bronze spears of the same type, although the archaeological yield from Assyria itself in this period is extremely thin, and the excavated copper spearheads come mostly from neighbouring sites such as Tell Billa and Hasanlu, and can serve as parallel evidence rather than direct proof. The ordinary equipment of Assyria in this period can be reconstructed in outline from the artefact types: a copper axe with a narrow blade and a wooden haft for cutting; copper daggers and short curved swords for work at close quarters; composite bows, which already existed in Mesopotamia, with arrowheads of copper or bone, though few actual examples come from Assyrian territory, which suggests that long-range firepower still rested on throwing weapons and light missiles; and shields, mostly wooden faced with hide and round in shape, the tall shield being rare as yet. There was as yet no organised armour and no helmet: Assyrian bronze helmets appear in quantity only in the Neo-Assyrian period, in royal tombs and on the reliefs. As for siege equipment, references to the siege and capture of towns survive in the Syrian documents from Emar and elsewhere, mentioning earthen ramps, battering rams and fire, but the civil war itself left no detail of any siege. In Assyria horses were still used chiefly for draught and riding, the light two-wheeled chariot being the standard of the Mesopotamian nobility, the number of horses in the army was limited, and cavalry was not the decisive arm. As for transport, the caravans of the Old Assyrian period moved between Anatolia and Assyria on donkey trains, each stage of about a hundred kilometres; by the years of the civil war the trade in copper and tin had already been cut off as Hurrian power pushed north, and that bears directly on how the armies could be re-equipped.
tactics: 這一役的戰術幾乎無從重建，只能從時代的做法與殘存文本推想。內戰的勝負關鍵在城而非野地：奪取阿舒爾並在聖城完成加冕，等於取得王位的合法性，因此雙方兵鋒指向城市，而攻城依賴的不是野戰器械而是圍困與城內的接應。亞述王室銘文常用的公式——「城不為他開」、城邑轉向另一方、人數被斬首計數——顯示內戰的常見結束方式是城邑倒戈或被攻破。野戰方面，這一時期兩河的常規打法是密集步兵配合輕裝步與弓手，銅矛手在前列成排，斧兵與弓手在後；馬茲王系與尼斯王系各有自己的核心區與徵召地，兵員多為城邑民兵與遊牧部落的臨時徵召，而非常備軍，因此出戰往往在收穫季前後、徵糧與兵源都吃緊的時節。糧秣方面，亞述心臟地有底格里斯河與支流可資運輸，但城郊一應食糧仍靠就地徵發，內戰中此起彼伏的燒掠往往切斷對方的田禾與倉儲，讓占領者自己也得挨餓。另一個關鍵是外交與宣傳：交戰雙方都需要外部承認，因此內戰期間對外往來、盟約與信使往還異常頻繁，一封信即可改變內戰的平衡。聖城、宮殿與要塞的守備由王室近衛與外族雇兵承擔，宮中衛兵的身分與忠誠，往往比城牆更能決定王位歸屬——阿舒爾-貝尼-伊提之死，據說就出於宮廷內部。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this engagement can hardly be reconstructed and can only be inferred from the practice of the age and from the few surviving texts. The issue of the war lay in cities rather than in open ground: to take Assur and to be crowned in the sacred city was to acquire the legitimacy of the throne, so the armies of both houses pointed at towns, and siege depended on blockade and on collusion inside the walls rather than on field artillery. The usual formulas of Assyrian royal inscriptions, such as his city did not open to him, the city turned away to the other side, and the count of those beheaded, show that the common way for a civil war to end was the defection or the capture of a town. In the field, the routine method of the period in Mesopotamia was dense infantry supported by light foot and archers, the spearmen in the front rank in rows, axe-men and archers behind. Each of the two houses had its own core area and its own recruiting grounds, and the soldiers were in the main the militia of the towns and levies hastily raised from the nomadic tribes rather than a standing army, so campaigns tended to fall before and after the harvest, when both the grain levy and the manpower were tight. As for supply, the Assyrian heartland had the Tigris and its tributaries for transport, but food for the suburbs still had to be requisitioned on the spot, and the mutual burning and raiding of the civil war repeatedly cut the enemy's crops and granaries, leaving the occupier hungry as well. The second key was diplomacy and propaganda. Both parties needed recognition from outside, so foreign contacts, alliances and the exchange of messengers were unusually busy during the civil war, and a single letter could shift the balance of the contest. The defence of the sacred city, the palace and the fortresses was entrusted to the royal guard and to foreign mercenaries, and the loyalty of the palace guard often mattered more to the fate of the throne than the walls did: Ashur-beni-iti's death, it is said, came from within the palace.
data: 可核對的數字有四類。第一是年代：本目錄把此役繫於公元前1732年，學界一般把亞述的雙王並立期放在約前1760年代至前1725年，長約四十五年，主要依據是王表與尼尼微出土的兩塊石碑的年代序列。第二是距離：亞述聖城阿舒爾（泰爾沙爾卡特）至馬茲約一百五十至二百公里，至尼努瓦（泰爾巴塞特基）約四百公里，至哈蘭約三百公里，至馬爾（泰爾哈里里）約三百五十公里，至巴比倫約五百公里；兩端同時進攻的話，距離與補給比作戰本身更吃緊。第三是考古：舊亞述時期亞述城邦的發掘極少，泰爾巴塞特基與哈薩努的出土物只能作旁證；安納托利亞的卡內什（庫爾泰佩）商埠在約前1750年前後被毀，顯示商路崩潰與內戰年代重疊。第四是人口與兵力：這一時期沒有任何可靠的兵力數字，王室碑刻與書信沿用「無數」「全地之兵」一類修辭，馬茲與尼斯兩系的實際兵力估計都在數千人至一萬餘之間，遠低於後世新亞述時期的部隊規模；任何寫出「亞述內戰雙方各出數萬精兵」的說法都應當打折扣。
dataEn: The checkable numbers fall into four classes. The first is chronology: this catalogue ties the war to 1732 BC, while scholarship generally places the period of the two kings of Assyria between about the 1760s and 1725 BC, a span of some forty-five years, deduced mainly from the king list and from the sequence of the two stelae excavated at Nineveh. The second is distance: from the sacred city of Assur, modern Tell Sherqat, to Mazi is about a hundred and fifty to two hundred kilometres, to Ninuua, modern Tell Bassetki, about four hundred, to Harran about three hundred, to Mari, modern Tell Hariri, about three hundred and fifty, and to Babylon about five hundred; an army advancing from both ends at once would have found distance and supply more troublesome than the fighting itself. The third is archaeology: excavation of the Assyrian city-states of the Old Assyrian period is very limited, and the finds at Tell Bassetki and Hasanlu can only serve as parallel evidence; the Anatolian trading post of Kanesh, modern Kultepe, was destroyed around 1750 BC, which shows the collapse of the trade routes overlapping with the years of the civil war. The fourth is population and numbers of men: no reliable figure for the armies of this period survives, royal inscriptions and letters use stock formulas such as countless and the troops of the whole land, and the actual strength of the two houses is estimated at somewhere between a few thousand and a little over ten thousand men, far below the scale of the armies of the later Neo-Assyrian period. Any statement that tens of thousands of regulars fought on each side in the Assyrian civil war should be heavily discounted.
cause: 內戰的成因可分三層。最深的一層是王權的雙重性：沙姆希-阿達德一世建立的那套跨幼發拉底與安納托利亞的商路帝國，在他死後崩解，兒子伊什梅-達甘一世未能收拾局面，其後裔分裂成兩支，各自佔據美索不達米亞北部的不同據點，亞述王位從此有兩條繼承線索，這是制度性的病竈。第二層是資源的斷裂：亞述早期王國的富裕建立在安納托利亞的銅錫礦與商埠網絡上，商埠在約前1750年前後陸續被毀或被胡里人控制，國王失去錫料來源，銅器與箭鏈的供應立刻吃緊；同時西部的幼發拉底各城邦、亞姆哈德王國與米坦尼都在擴張，把亞述往北推，亞述心臟地反而成了最安全也最貧瘠的退守之地。第三層是外部的趁火打劫：亞姆哈德與哈納國等地看見亞述內部分裂，紛紛侵吞河間地與哈布拉河一帶的附庸城。直接導火線在文獻中沒有留下。最合理的重建是：阿舒爾-貝尼-伊提承襲王位後，馬茲王系與尼斯王系之間的王位爭奪同時爆發，亞馬尼-貝尼-阿達德以宗族權力挑戰正統並奪取王位，內戰隨即在阿舒爾與其周邊展開；一方守著聖城與王系祖地，一方握著由阿舒爾-馬基爾一系經營的西北方據點，兩邊都不能承受對方存在，於是內戰拖成整整一代人的消耗。
causeEn: The causes of the civil war fall into three layers. The deepest is the duality of the kingship: the trading empire that Shamshi-Adad I had built across the Euphrates and Anatolia fell apart after his death, and his son Ishme-Dagan I failed to repair it; his descendants split into two branches, each holding a different seat in northern Mesopotamia, and from that moment the Assyrian throne had two lines of succession, a structural fault in the constitution. The second layer is the severance of resources: the wealth of the early Assyrian kingdom had rested on the copper and tin of Anatolia and on a network of trading posts, and those posts were destroyed one after another around 1750 BC or were taken over by the Hurrians, so the king lost his tin supply and the fitting out of copper vessels and arrowheads became hard at once. At the same time the Euphrates city-states, the kingdom of Yamhad and Mitanni were all expanding in the west and pushing Assyria north, leaving the Assyrian heartland the safest place to hold but the poorest to live in. The third layer is the temptation of the neighbours: seeing Assyria split, Yamhad and the small states around Khana began to swallow the vassal towns of the middle Euphrates and the Khabur. No document records the immediate occasion. The most reasonable reconstruction is that after Ashur-beni-iti took the throne the contest between the Mazi and Nis houses broke out, that Yamani-beni-Adad challenged the legitimate succession with the authority of his clan and seized the kingship, and that the civil war then opened around Assur and its neighbourhood. One side held the sacred city and the ancestral seat of the royal house, the other held the north-western positions built up by the line of Ashur-makir, and neither could afford to let the other exist, so the war dragged on for a whole generation of attrition.
impact: 內戰的直接後果是亞述王室的整合：以阿舒爾-尼拉里一世為中心，雙王並立終於結束，亞述恢復一個王、一套年表、一次加冕的秩序，這套秩序一直延續到前十一世紀的新亞述時期，成為後來亞述能向黎凡特與安納托利亞擴張的組織基礎。另一面的後果是國力與國際地位的流失：內戰年代的亞述在西部完全失去主動權，幼發拉底中游的城邦與哈布拉河流域落入亞姆哈德與後來米坦尼的勢力範圍，亞述人要再等到前十五世紀才重新向那一帶伸出軍力。第三是史料意義：哈納努致亞述王的書信是「亞述雙王並立」最著名的物證，尼尼微出土的阿舒爾-貝尼-伊提與亞馬尼-貝尼-阿達德兩塊石碑，則是前二千年亞述唯一一批王室紀念碑，兩塊碑同出一地並互為對立，構成罕見的雙方自述材料，後世對亞述早期國王的年表重建幾乎全靠這幾件東西。第四是對亞述自身歷史記憶的影響：亞述王室後來把城邦時代的國王視為先王的序列，這場內戰中的奪位與弒逆被吸收進王權神聖性的敘事，國王「蒙阿舒爾護佑」的說法，就是從這個時期開始成形。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the civil war was the reunification of the Assyrian royal house: centred on Ashur-nirari I the two kingship came to an end, and Assyria recovered an order of one king, one chronology and one coronation, an order that ran on into the Neo-Assyrian period of the eleventh century BC and became the organisational base from which Assyria would later expand towards the Levant and Anatolia. On the other side, the war cost the kingdom strength and standing abroad: in the west Assyria lost all initiative during these years, the towns of the middle Euphrates and the Khabur basin passed into the sphere of Yamhad and later Mitanni, and Assyria did not extend military power in that direction again until the fifteenth century BC. The third consequence is evidential. The letter of Hananu to the king of Assyria is the best known document for the twofold kingship of Assyria, and the two stelae of Ashur-beni-iti and Yamani-beni-Adad from Nineveh are the only body of royal commemorative monuments that Assyria of the second millennium has yielded. The two stelae come from the same site and stand against each other, and together they form a rare piece of self-testimony from both sides; almost the whole later reconstruction of the chronology of the early Assyrian kings rests on these few objects. The fourth is the effect on Assyrian historical memory. The royal house of the later period treated the city-state kings as a sequence of ancestors, and the usurpation and the killing of the civil war were absorbed into the narrative of the sacredness of kingship: the notion that the king is guarded by Ashur begins to take shape in this period.
result: 內戰的過程只能從殘存的幾件材料推想，順序大致是：亞馬尼-貝尼-阿達德先勝——他起兵反叛，殺死在位者阿舒爾-貝尼-伊提，奪取王位；但他的統治不穩，尼斯王系的阿舒爾-尼拉里一世（伊什梅-卡利-盧）隨後起兵，攻回王位並擊敗亞馬尼-貝尼-阿達德，亞馬尼本人下落不明，或死於戰陣，或事後被處置。阿舒爾-尼拉里一世在位後，亞述不再有第二個王，內戰至此結束，前1725年前後亞述重新回到單一王權。因此就勝負而言，馬茲王系輸掉了這場戰爭，尼斯王系贏得了它；但兩系的王統最終合流，阿舒爾-尼拉里一世後裔的亞述王室在後來被視為沙姆希-阿達德一系的正統延續，內戰的分裂痕跡被抹平。若以版圖論，內戰沒有給亞述帶來任何土地擴張，反而丟失了大片西部的附庸與商路利益；它的真實贏家是亞姆哈德與胡里系的小國，它們在亞述內耗的同時擴大了自己的緩衝區。一場沒有外敵的戰爭，成為亞述由商路帝國轉為保守核心國的轉折點。
resultEn: The course of the war can only be inferred from the few surviving objects, and the order of events was roughly as follows: Yamani-beni-Adad won the first round, rising in revolt, killing the reigning Ashur-beni-iti and taking the throne; but his rule was insecure, and Ashur-nirari I of the Nis house, Ishme-kali-lu, then rose in his turn, carried the throne back and defeated Yamani-beni-Adad, whose fate afterwards is unknown, either he fell in the fighting or was disposed of afterwards. Once Ashur-nirari I was on the throne there was no second king in Assyria, the civil war was over, and around 1725 BC Assyria returned to a single kingship. So as to the issue of the war, the Mazi house lost it and the Nis house won it; the two lines of descent nonetheless finally merged, and the Assyrian royal house descended from Ashur-nirari I was later treated as the legitimate continuation of the line of Shamshi-Adad I, and the traces of the split were smoothed away. Judged in terms of territory, the civil war brought Assyria no expansion at all and cost it the vassal towns and the trading interests of much of the west; its real winners were Yamhad and the small Hurrian states, which enlarged their own buffer zones while Assyria consumed itself. A war without an external enemy became the turning point at which Assyria changed from a trading empire into a conservative core state.
